minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 8, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:01 p.m., on March 8, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 3, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:34 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Ury declared the meeting recessed. The City Council reconvened
at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

City Council Minutes  1  March 8, 2016
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the Saddleback College Football Team as Southern California Football
  Association Champions and Recognize Coach Mark McElroy for being named
  American Community College Football Coaches Association (ACCFCA) Coach of the
  Year

  Mayor Ury presented the proclamation to Coach McElroy, the Assistant Coaches and the
  Saddleback College Football Team players.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Ury

17.  Consideration of a City Investment in the Santa Margarita Water District Advanced
  Purified Water Treatment Facility

  Mayor Ury took item 17 out of order so that representatives of Lake Mission Viejo could
  speak on the matter early since their own Board Meeting will be held later in the evening.

  Kevin Frabotta, General Manager of Lake Mission Viejo Association, M.V.: urged the City
  Council to seriously consider the City's financial participation in the project.

  Kevin Pennington, President of the Lake Mission Viejo Association Board of Directors,
  M.V.: discussed the proposed Advance Purified Water Treatment Facility at Lake Mission
  Viejo and asked that the City become a partner in the innovative water supply sustainability
  project.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: expressed concern with the high price of gasoline in California and asked the
City Council what they can do about the problem.

Sohil Majdi, M.V.: asked the City Council to support a Persian parade in the City for celebration
of Nowruz.

Rhonda Reardon, representing Supervisor Patricia Bates: reminded residents that Senior Day 2016
will be held Friday, March 11 at the Murray Community Center and on Wednesday, March 9,
Mission Viejo Christian Church will host a program on marijuana and protection of our youth.

Jacklyn Flowers, M.V.: thanked the Council for the proclamation regarding the International Day
of Happiness and extended an invitation to the celebration which will be held on Saturday, March
12, 2016, from 11:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center.

City Council Minutes  2  March 8, 2016
 Eileen Gonzalez, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for the new street lights on Muirlands
Boulevard.

Victor Gonzalez, M.V.: thanked City staff for cleaning up and securing the property at the former
Haggens grocery store.

Hannah Hess, representing Congresswoman Mimi Walters, M.V.: announced that
Congresswoman Walters is hosting a program on cyber security and identity protection on March
24, 2016, at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

7.  2015 Residential Resurfacing-CDBG Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP
  838)-Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

8.  Maintenance of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Flashing Beacons,
  Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights and CCTV Cameras-Contract
  Extension

City Council Minutes  3  March 8, 2016
   Approved Fourth Amendment to Contract A12-01 with Siemens Industry, Inc., extending
  the term of the contract to June 30, 2016.

9.  Muirlands Boulevard Street Light Installation (CIP 222)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

10.  Request by the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library for a one-time exemption to the
  "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities

  Approved request by the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library for a one-time exemption to
  the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

STAFF REPORTS

14.  Status Report on Proposed State Legislation Related to Regulating Sober Living
  Homes

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  The following expressed concerns with residential sober living homes in Mission
  Viejo: Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.; Tom Coyle, M.V.; Peggy Russo, M.V.; Natalia Noacek, M.V.;
  Bill Gire, M.V.; Jarrett Mahoney, M.V.; Mary Mayes, M.V.; and Parisa Houshangi, M.V.

  The following commented on the need for good sober living homes: Thomas Miller, M.V.

  Residents were invited to a Town Hall meeting on March 29, 2016, from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m.
  in the City Council chamber which will be held solely to address this topic.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended for item 16 (page 5) to reflect
  her concern with "increased delays for cross traffic at intersections" and for item 17 (page
  6) that the Council did not have enough information to make a sound decision "based on a
  survey for 2008."

City Council Minutes  4  March 8, 2016
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 23, 2016, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

3.  Check Register Dated February 12, 2016 in the Amount of $422,611.99

  Council Member Schlicht asked about payments made to Direct TV.

  City Manager Wilberg responded that staff made the change from Cox Cable to Direct TV
  at city facilities because there was a cost savings.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated February 19, 2016 in the Amount of $2,209,684.82

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is opposed to the City's membership in the Orange
  County Business Council (OCBC) because they endorse political candidates. She also
  asked about a payment to RJM for consulting services for Lot C field services."

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the City
  needed an independent grading analysis to understand the potential for building on Site C.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  March 8, 2016
 5.  Purchase of Two (2) Replacement Police Services Motorcycles

  Council Member Schlicht stated that back in June she said that the City should be looking
  at ways to reduce the Sheriff's Department contract and it is her preference that the
  motorcycles be traded for cruisers. She further recommended that the Council hold a
  discussion on the benefits or motorcycles versus cars.

  Council Member Sachs reiterated his opinion that staff should be looking into leasing the
  vehicles versus purchasing and he noted that he will continue to bring that up.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  a purchase order with Irv Seaver Motorcycles, Inc. in the amount of $55,969.80 for the
  purchase of two (2) 2016 BMW Police Motorcycles.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

6.  General Plan Progress Report 2015

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is not happy with the historical write up for the
  UDR project in the staff report and asked that it be clarified that the Housing Authority,
  not the City, owns the land known as Site C. Regarding the dog park, she asked that it be
  noted that the City traded 6 acres to get 4 acres. Council Member Schlicht asked the City
  Attorney if AB 1826 will require the City or the County to provide a restaurant organics
  diversion program on or before April 1, 2016, and she asked staff whether or not there is a
  fee for the City's Green Business Program. Lastly, Council Member Schlicht asked staff to
  provide the Council with the names of the two priority projects and eleven non-priority
  projects that may be a threat to the waterways.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to receive
  and file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

11.  Appeal filed by Ryan Farsai of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s
  approval of Conditional Use Permit CUP2015-343, Minor Modification MM2015-
City Council Minutes  6  March 8, 2016
   354, and Variance VAR2015-44, petitions submitted by Ryan Farsai to permit the
  renovation of an existing Arco gas station located at 25122 Marguerite Parkway, in
  the CC (Commercial Community) zone. CUP2015-343 is filed for expansion of the
  existing convenience store and for a Type 21 Alcohol Beverage Control (ABC) license
  allowing off-sales of beer, wine and distilled spirits. MM2015-354 is filed for site
  improvements including revised parking and landscape, and exterior building
  improvements including the expanded convenience store and a new smog-test bay, all
  with an updated architectural theme. VAR2015-44 is filed for reduced building
  setbacks along the site frontage with Marguerite Parkway and La Paz Road

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ury opened the public hearing at 7:50 p.m.

  Ryan Farsai, owner of the ARCO gas station at 25122 Marguerite Parkway, M.V.:
  presented his case for the Conditional Use Permit, the Minor Modification and the
  Variance. Mr. Farsai requested a continuance of the public hearing so that he can work
  with a subcommittee of the Council.

  Hamid Farsai, M.V.: expressed support for the expansion of the convenience store to
  include the sale of beer, wine and distilled spirits.

  The following spoke in support of the applicant and provided clarification on questions
  posed during the public hearing: William K. (Bill) Koska, Attorney for Mr. Farsai, Poway;
  and Rick A. Blake, Attorney for Mr. Farsai, Santa Ana.

  Applicant Ryan Farsai provided rebuttal comments.

  At the hour of 8:52 p.m., Mayor Ury closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to
  approve the appeal and approve Conditional Use Permit CUP2015-343, Minor
  Modification MM2015-354, and Variance VAR2015-44, being an appeal filed by Ryan
  Farsai of the Planning and Transportation Commission's October 12, 2015, approval of
  Conditional Use Permit CUP2015-343, Minor Modification MM2015-354, and Variance
  VAR2015-44, to permit the renovation of an existing Arco Gas Station located at 25122
  Marguerite Parkway, in the CC (Commercial Community) Zone.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Schlicht and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  March 8, 2016
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to uphold the
  Planning and Transportation Commission’s position regarding title and fee structure for
  the easement on the property.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

12.  Animal Services Proposals for the Cities of Rancho Santa Margarita and Laguna Hills

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented staff report.

  The following spoke in favor of the City of Mission Viejo offering proposals and
  potentially providing animal services to the cities of Rancho Santa Margarita and Laguna
  Hills: Laura Johnson, M.V.; Sharon Cody, M.V.; and Robert D. Breton, M.V.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to
  authorize City Staff to send the Draft Agreement, MOU, and Cost Analysis Proposal for
  Animal Services to the Cities of Rancho Santa Margarita and Laguna Hills respectively for
  review and consideration.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

17.  Consideration of a City Investment in the Santa Margarita Water District Advanced
  Purified Water Treatment Facility

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

  Dan Ferrons, General Manager, Santa Margarita Water District: stated that this is an
  innovative project and would be the first time in the State of California that a recreational
  swimming lake would be filled with advanced purified recycled water.

  By consensus, the Council (1) called for a special meeting of the Investment Advisory
  Commission for the purpose of considering the investment possibility for this proposal;
  and (2) created a small ad-hoc committee comprised of Mayor Ury and Council Member
  Sachs to consider this matter further.

City Council Minutes  8  March 8, 2016
 RECESS

At the hour of 9:58 p.m., Mayor Ury declared the meeting recessed. The City Council reconvened
at 10:07 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury announced that there has not been a meeting of the OCTA Board since the last
  City Council meeting so he had nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager Wilberg drew the Council’s attention to the monthly status report on the Aquatics
Center renovation. He asked the Council Members to take a look at it and let him know if it
provides enough summary information or if they would like additional details. He highlighted that
staff expects that the construction documents will be 50% complete by the end of the week and he
introduced John Hughes, the Project Manager with Griffin Structures.

15.  Mission Viejo Police Services 2015 Year-End Crime Statistics Report

  Lieutenant Brad NewMyer presented the report and answered the City Council Members
  questions.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that he did not have any comments.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that he did not have any comments.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that due to the time, she didn’t express her feelings about the
animal shelter earlier. She said that she doesn’t believe that it’s in the best interests of Mission
City Council Minutes  9  March 8, 2016
 Viejo to expand the size and scope of its government to help another city reduce the size and scope
of their government. She stated that the lobbyists from those cities should be lobbying their
government, not Mission Viejo. Council member Schlicht said that she would still like staff to
look into leasing space at the animal shelter so taxpayers do not have to carry the burden of the pit
of pensions. She asked God to bless Nancy Reagan, a woman of class, dignity and elegance, who
passed away and is now together with President Reagan again. Council Member Schlicht
recognized hero Edward Byers who recently received the Medal of Honor. She said that he is a
humble man who believes that the true hero was Nic Checque, a soldier killed during the 2012
operation in Afghanistan. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from
Edward Byers: “He (Checque) died a warrior and he died to bring back another American. I
believe that our nation owes him a debt of gratitude. He lived his life as a warrior and he carried
out the toughest mission selflessly, fearlessly. He made the ultimate sacrifice that day.”

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum announced that she enjoyed attending several Little League opening
nights over the past two weeks. She noted that it was also an honor to represent the City in
Sacramento at the Orange County Business Council (OCBC) joint trip with the Association of
California Cities-Orange County (ACC-OC.) Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum said good work is being
done and she brought back her packets which have great information and resources and she said
she’d be happy to share them with anyone who is interested. She announced that she will be
present at the Town Hall meeting on sober living homes on March 29 and the International Day of
Happiness celebration, March 12. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum encouraged residents to attend
Senator Pat Bates’ Senior Day event on March 11 and Congresswoman Mimi Walters Cyber
Security and Identify Protection forum on March 24. Lastly, to clear up any potential
misconceptions after statements made earlier in the meeting, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum discussed
the City’s historical support of Nowruz celebrations in the community.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury noted that there have been recent discussions regarding the merging of the two toll
road agencies and that is now eminent so he will appoint Council Member Sachs to serve on the
new single Board. He stated that the Orange County Business Council (OCBC) trip to Sacramento
was very interesting. There were a lot of good speakers and the highlight was the evening when
they mingled with legislators and focused on the topics of transportation, the environment and the
economy. Mayor Ury said that the President of the Senate spoke about how he is planning the
new economy with SB 350 and when Council Member Ury asked him what he is doing to keep
younger kids in California, somehow the Senator turned that into a speech about solar panels and
the EPA rating for trucks in Alabama. Mayor Ury said that he never got an answer to his question
but he continues to be concerned about the unaffordability of California for young adults.

City Council Minutes  10  March 8, 2016
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:29 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Bette Lindsey, to Tuesday, March 22, 2016, at
5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 22, 2016

City Council Minutes  11  March 8, 2016
